title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck builds the divided-power (PD) envelope Gamma(A,J) of a ring A with ideal J. It is the universal pair (A',J') with divided powers that receives a map (A,J) -> (A',J'). He builds it as a quotient of Gamma_A^+(J), then forms an extension of A/J. He notes that if A is a Lambda-algebra, so is Gamma(A,J). This page has two items.

(1) Special case. Take A = Sym_Lambda(M), the symmetric algebra of a Lambda-module M, and J = Sym^+_Lambda(M), its augmentation ideal. A map of pairs (Sym M, Sym^+ M) -> (B, I) into a Lambda-algebra B with PD ideal I is the same thing as a Lambda-linear map M -> I. So the universal problem becomes: send M into a Lambda-algebra with divided powers. Its solution is the divided power algebra Gamma_Lambda(M) of Roby, with PD ideal Gamma^+_Lambda(M). Hence Gamma(Sym_Lambda M, Sym^+_Lambda M) is isomorphic to (Gamma_Lambda(M), Gamma^+_Lambda(M)).

Grothendieck then draws a consequence. Gamma_Lambda(M), as a ring with PD ideal, depends functorially on the augmented algebra Sym_Lambda(M), not only on M. Any morphism of augmented Lambda-algebras Sym M -> Sym N induces a PD morphism Gamma(M) -> Gamma(N). Such morphisms are, e.g., polynomial maps without constant term. So Gamma is functorial for non-linear maps.

(2) Quotients of PD rings. Let (A,J,gamma) be a ring with PD ideal and x_i, i in I, elements of J. Find the universal PD morphism (A,J) -> (A',J') killing the x_i. Answer: A' = A/K, where K is the ideal generated by the gamma_n(x_i), n >= 1. Elements of K are the sums of lambda_{n,i} gamma_n(x_i) with lambda in A.
- K is the smallest ideal stable under the gamma_n that contains the x_i, i.e. the sub-PD ideal they generate.
- Stability check: gamma_m(lambda gamma_n(x)) = lambda^m ((mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)) gamma_{mn}(x), plus the sum formula.
- On the next page he adds: for such K, and only such K, the gamma_n descend to (A/K, J/K).

The margin note 'plus haut avec B', avec fonctorialités' is a reminder to redo the earlier construction with functorialities. The next page goes on to nilpotent PD ideals and the exp/log isomorphisms between 1+J and J.
errors: No real errors. In (2), descent of the PD structure to A/K needs K∩J to be a sub-PD ideal; here K ⊂ J because the x_i are taken in J, so this holds. If x_i outside J were allowed, the statement would need modifying (one would need K∩J to be a sub-PD ideal).

The displayed isomorphism should read Gamma(Sym M, Sym^+ M) ≅ Gamma_Lambda(M), with PD ideal Gamma^+_Lambda(M). The left side is the whole envelope ring, not only its ideal. Depending on the reading of the superscript (+ or *), the notation is slightly loose.

ideas.what: The PD envelope of the augmentation ideal of Sym_Lambda(M) is the divided power algebra Gamma_Lambda(M)
ideas.modern_name: Divided power envelope D_{Sym M}(Sym^+ M) ≅ Gamma(M); universal property of Roby's Gamma
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963-65) for Gamma(M) and its universal property; Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (1974), Ch. I, for PD envelopes
ideas.where_published: Roby, 'Lois polynômes et lois formelles en théorie des modules' (1963) and 'Les algèbres à puissances divisées' (1965); Berthelot, LNM 407

ideas.what: Gamma_Lambda(M) is functorial in the augmented algebra Sym M, i.e. for polynomial (non-linear) maps without constant term
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of divided power algebras for polynomial laws

ideas.what: Quotient of a PD ring by the sub-PD ideal generated by elements: the ideal generated by all gamma_n(x_i)
ideas.modern_name: Sub-PD ideal generated by a set; PD quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (1974, Ch. I, §1-2); Berthelot-Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology (1978)
ideas.where_published: Berthelot LNM 407; Stacks Project, tag on divided power ideals

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational material on divided power envelopes and PD quotients. It was written up systematically by Berthelot shortly afterwards, building on Roby. Nothing here goes beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: Displayed formula: the image reads Gamma(Sym_Lambda(M), Sym^+_Lambda(M)) ≅ Gamma^*_Lambda(M) (or Gamma_Lambda(M)), i.e. the full graded divided power algebra rather than Gamma^+.

'augmenté Sym^+_Lambda(M)' is likely 'augmenté Sym^*_Lambda(M)' / 'l'anneau augmenté Sym_Lambda(M)'. The phrase reads roughly: 'Gamma_Lambda(M) dépend fonctoriellement de l'anneau augmenté Sym_Lambda(M)'.
'trouver les lois (A,J) -> (A',J')' is likely 'trouver les homomorphismes (A,J) -> (A',J')'.
'F-ière [?] en (A',J') universelle ? Ici' is plausibly 'Existe-t-il un (A',J') universel ? Oui,'.
'sum lambda_{n,i} pi^n(x_i)' has crossed-out terms. 'i.e. les expressions' is followed by 'avec lambda_{n,i} ∈ A'.
Margin: 'plus haut avec B', avec fonctorialités.....' (reading uncertain; possibly 'voir plus haut').
